matches.note: R2 says confirm never inspects the bytes, so arbitrary content can be stored under the image type the client declared.
No reported finding mentions objects left in the bucket after a rejected confirm.
R3 mentions octet-stream only as context for a different defect; nothing flags the default allow-list itself.
Nothing reported covers free-text entity names that skip the ownership check.
R4 identifies the prefix-only check in saveStep5, which lets unconfirmed, wrong-type or '..' keys through.

unmatched_reported.note: The presigned PUT stays valid after confirm and is not bound to a content length, so a second PUT can replace the confirmed object and get around the recorded size and quota.
The confirm event listener sets photo_url for any confirmed coach_profile key without checking content type or size, a separate path from saveStep5.
Reconfirming an older key inside the TTL window re-fires the event, and the unconditional UPDATE puts the older photo back.
